questions.text: In which year did Sir Syed Ahmad Khan die?
questions.explanation: Sir Syed died on 27 March 1898 at Aligarh and was buried beside the mosque of the college he had founded.

questions.text: The Muhammadan Anglo-Oriental College at Aligarh was established in which year?
questions.explanation: Sir Syed opened the school at Aligarh in 1875, which was raised to the status of a college in 1877.

questions.text: Which book did Sir Syed Ahmad Khan write to explain the causes of the 1857 uprising?
questions.explanation: In Asbab-e-Baghawat-e-Hind Sir Syed argued that British ignorance of Indian feeling, not Muslim disloyalty, had caused the revolt.

questions.text: Sir Syed Ahmad Khan launched the magazine Tahzib-ul-Akhlaq in which year?
questions.explanation: Tahzib-ul-Akhlaq was started in 1870 to promote social and intellectual reform among Indian Muslims.

questions.text: Sir Syed Ahmad Khan founded the Scientific Society in 1864 at which place?
questions.explanation: The Scientific Society was established at Ghazipur in 1864 to translate Western works on science into Urdu, and was later moved to Aligarh.

questions.text: The Urdu-Hindi controversy of 1867, which deepened Sir Syed's belief in Muslim separateness, began in which city?
questions.explanation: A movement at Banaras in 1867 demanded that Hindi in Devanagari script replace Urdu in the courts, convincing Sir Syed that Hindus and Muslims could not remain one nation.

questions.text: The Muhammadan Educational Conference was founded by Sir Syed Ahmad Khan in which year?
questions.explanation: Founded in 1886, the Muhammadan Educational Conference met annually across India to spread modern education among Muslims and later provided the platform on which the Muslim League was formed.

questions.text: Which Viceroy ordered the partition of Bengal in 1905?
questions.explanation: Lord Curzon carried out the partition of Bengal on administrative grounds, dividing a province that was too large to govern effectively.

questions.text: The partition of Bengal took effect on 16 October of which year?
questions.explanation: The partition became effective on 16 October 1905, a day observed by Hindu opponents as a day of mourning.

questions.text: What was the capital of the new province of Eastern Bengal and Assam created in 1905?
questions.explanation: Dacca became the capital of Eastern Bengal and Assam, giving the Muslim-majority east its own administrative centre.

questions.text: In which year was the partition of Bengal annulled?
questions.explanation: The partition was reversed in 1911 in the face of sustained Hindu agitation, which convinced Muslims that British assurances were unreliable.

questions.text: Which Muslim leader of Dacca was the strongest supporter of the partition of Bengal?
questions.explanation: Nawab Salimullah Khan of Dacca championed the partition because it gave the Muslims of eastern Bengal an administration of their own.

questions.text: The Simla Deputation waited upon the Viceroy on 1 October of which year?
questions.explanation: The deputation of Muslim notables met the Viceroy at Simla on 1 October 1906, three months before the Muslim League was founded.

questions.text: Who led the Simla Deputation of 1906?
questions.explanation: Sir Aga Khan III headed the deputation and read the address presented to the Viceroy.

questions.text: How many members made up the Simla Deputation of 1906?
questions.explanation: Thirty-five Muslim leaders drawn from all provinces of India formed the deputation that met Lord Minto.

questions.text: The central demand of the Simla Deputation was for
options: Urdu as the official language of India
the abolition of the zamindari system
questions.explanation: The deputation asked that Muslims be given separate electorates and weightage in representation because of their political importance, a demand conceded in 1909.

questions.text: The All India Muslim League was founded on 30 December of which year?
questions.explanation: The League was founded on 30 December 1906 during the annual session of the Muhammadan Educational Conference.

questions.text: In which city was the All India Muslim League founded?
questions.explanation: The League was founded at Dacca, where the Muhammadan Educational Conference was holding its annual session.

questions.text: Who was the first President of the All India Muslim League?
questions.explanation: Sir Aga Khan III was chosen as the first President of the League and held the office until 1912.

questions.text: The London branch of the All India Muslim League was established in 1908 by
questions.explanation: Syed Ameer Ali set up the League's London branch in 1908 to present the Muslim case before British opinion.

questions.text: Muhammad Ali Jinnah formally joined the All India Muslim League in which year?
questions.explanation: Jinnah joined the League in 1913 after it adopted self-government as its aim, while retaining his Congress membership for some years.

questions.text: Muhammad Ali Jinnah was born on 25 December of which year?
questions.explanation: Jinnah was born at Karachi on 25 December 1876.

questions.text: Jinnah was first elected to the Imperial Legislative Council in 1910 as a Muslim member from
questions.explanation: Jinnah entered the Imperial Legislative Council in 1910 as the Muslim member for Bombay.

questions.text: Which measure did Jinnah pilot through the Imperial Legislative Council in 1913 to protect Muslim family endowments?
questions.explanation: Jinnah secured passage of the Mussalman Wakf Validating Act, commonly called the Wakf Alal Aulad Act, restoring the legality of family endowments.

questions.text: The Lucknow Pact was concluded in which year?
questions.explanation: The Congress and the Muslim League concluded the Lucknow Pact in December 1916 on a joint scheme of constitutional reform.

questions.text: Under the Lucknow Pact the Indian National Congress for the first time accepted
questions.explanation: The chief Muslim gain from the Lucknow Pact was Congress recognition of separate electorates and of weightage for Muslims in minority provinces.

questions.text: Who gave Jinnah the title 'Ambassador of Hindu-Muslim Unity'?
questions.explanation: Sarojini Naidu described Jinnah as the Ambassador of Hindu-Muslim Unity for his role in bringing about the Lucknow Pact.

questions.text: Who ordered the firing at Jallianwala Bagh?
questions.explanation: Brigadier-General Reginald Dyer commanded the troops that fired on the crowd at Jallianwala Bagh.

questions.text: The Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms of 1919 introduced which system in the provinces?
questions.explanation: The Government of India Act 1919 introduced dyarchy, dividing provincial subjects into reserved and transferred halves.

questions.text: The Khilafat Movement was launched in which year?
questions.explanation: The Khilafat Movement began in 1919 to defend the Ottoman Caliphate after the Turkish defeat in the First World War.

questions.text: The All India Khilafat Committee was formed in 1919 in which city?
questions.explanation: The All India Khilafat Committee was set up at Bombay in 1919 to organise the movement and raise funds for it.

questions.text: The 'Ali Brothers' of the Khilafat Movement were
options: Zafar Ali Khan and Shaukat Ali
Muhammad Ali Jauhar and Zafar Ali Khan
Muhammad Ali Jauhar and Shaukat Ali
Shaukat Ali and Syed Ameer Ali
questions.explanation: Maulana Muhammad Ali Jauhar and Maulana Shaukat Ali led the Khilafat agitation and were known as the Ali Brothers.

questions.text: The Hijrat Movement of 1920 involved the migration of Indian Muslims to
questions.explanation: Thousands of Muslims left for Afghanistan in 1920 after India was declared dar-ul-harb, but the migration ended in hardship and failure.

questions.text: The newspaper 'Al-Hilal' was launched in 1912 by
questions.explanation: Maulana Abul Kalam Azad brought out Al-Hilal from Calcutta in 1912, giving Urdu journalism a militant anti-British tone.

questions.text: The Simon Commission was appointed by the British government in which year?
questions.explanation: The commission was appointed in 1927 to review the working of the 1919 reforms and reached India in 1928.

questions.text: Indian parties boycotted the Simon Commission chiefly because
options: it recommended the partition of India
it proposed to abolish separate electorates
it was headed by a serving general
questions.explanation: All seven members of the commission were British, which Indians of every party resented as a denial of their fitness to shape their own constitution.

questions.text: The committee that produced the Nehru Report of 1928 was chaired by
questions.explanation: Motilal Nehru chaired the committee appointed by the All Parties Conference to draft a constitution for India.

questions.text: On the question of representation, the Nehru Report recommended
options: reservation of half the seats for Muslims
questions.explanation: The report proposed joint electorates with reservation in some cases, which Muslims saw as the withdrawal of the safeguard granted in 1909 and confirmed in 1916.

questions.text: Jinnah presented his Fourteen Points in which year?
questions.explanation: Jinnah placed the Fourteen Points before the Muslim League in March 1929 as the Muslim answer to the Nehru Report.

questions.text: One of Jinnah's Fourteen Points demanded that Muslim representation in the central legislature should not be less than
questions.explanation: The points required that Muslims be given not less than one-third of the seats in the central legislature.

questions.text: The Delhi Muslim Proposals were put forward by Jinnah in which year?
questions.explanation: In 1927 Jinnah offered to give up separate electorates in return for stated safeguards, an offer set aside after the Nehru Report.

questions.text: Allama Iqbal delivered his famous Allahabad Address in which year?
questions.explanation: Iqbal delivered the address in December 1930, outlining the idea of a consolidated Muslim state in north-western India.

questions.text: In the Allahabad Address Iqbal proposed the amalgamation of which areas into a single state?
options: Punjab, North-West Frontier Province, Sindh and Balochistan
questions.explanation: Iqbal called for the Punjab, the North-West Frontier Province, Sindh and Balochistan to be amalgamated into a single state.

questions.text: Allama Iqbal died on
questions.explanation: Iqbal died at Lahore on 21 April 1938, nine years before the state he had envisaged came into being.

questions.text: Allama Iqbal obtained his doctorate from a university in which city?
questions.explanation: Iqbal took his doctorate from the University of Munich in 1908 with a thesis on the development of metaphysics in Persia.

questions.text: Allama Iqbal was knighted in which year?
questions.explanation: Iqbal received a knighthood in 1922 in recognition of his poetry and scholarship.

questions.text: Which party boycotted the First Round Table Conference of 1930-31?
questions.explanation: The Congress stayed away from the First Round Table Conference because its leaders were in jail during the civil disobedience movement.

questions.text: Gandhi personally attended which Round Table Conference?
questions.explanation: Gandhi attended only the Second Round Table Conference of 1931 as the sole representative of the Congress.

questions.text: Gandhi's participation in the Second Round Table Conference followed which agreement?
questions.explanation: Under the Gandhi-Irwin Pact of March 1931 civil disobedience was suspended and the Congress agreed to attend the conference.

questions.text: The Third Round Table Conference was held in which year?
questions.explanation: The third and last conference met in London late in 1932 and was attended by only a small number of delegates.

questions.text: The Communal Award of 1932 was announced by the British Prime Minister
questions.explanation: Ramsay MacDonald announced the Communal Award in August 1932 after the Round Table Conferences failed to reach a communal settlement.

questions.text: The name 'Pakistan' was coined by
questions.explanation: Chaudhry Rahmat Ali coined the name in 1933 in a pamphlet issued from Cambridge.

questions.text: Chaudhry Rahmat Ali's pamphlet of 1933 in which the name Pakistan first appeared was titled
questions.explanation: The pamphlet Now or Never, issued on 28 January 1933, first used the word Pakistan for the Muslim homeland in north-western India.

questions.text: The Government of India Act 1935 introduced which system in the provinces?
options: Nomination of ministers by the Viceroy
questions.explanation: The Act of 1935 abolished provincial dyarchy and gave the provinces autonomy under ministers responsible to elected legislatures.

questions.text: Under the constitutional changes of the mid-1930s, Sindh was made a separate province by separating it from
questions.explanation: Sindh, long a part of the Bombay Presidency, became a separate province in 1936 under the Government of India Act 1935.

questions.text: The Muslim League observed the 'Day of Deliverance' on 22 December of which year?
questions.explanation: Jinnah called for a Day of Deliverance on 22 December 1939 after the Congress ministries resigned.

questions.text: The Pirpur Report of 1938 dealt with
options: Muslim grievances under the Congress ministries
the demarcation of the Punjab boundary
questions.explanation: The committee headed by Raja Syed Muhammad Mehdi of Pirpur inquired into Muslim complaints against the Congress provincial governments.

questions.text: The Sikandar-Jinnah Pact was concluded in which year?
questions.explanation: Sir Sikandar Hayat Khan agreed in 1937 that Muslim members of his Unionist Party would join the Muslim League, greatly strengthening it in the Punjab.

questions.text: A. K. Fazlul Haq was popularly known as
questions.explanation: Fazlul Haq, Premier of Bengal, was called Sher-e-Bengal, the Lion of Bengal.

questions.text: Jinnah returned permanently from England to India to reorganise the Muslim League in
questions.explanation: Jinnah gave up his London practice and returned in 1934, when he was elected permanent president of the Muslim League.

questions.text: Liaquat Ali Khan became Honorary General Secretary of the All India Muslim League in
questions.explanation: Liaquat Ali Khan was elected general secretary in 1936 and held the office until independence.

questions.text: The Lahore Resolution was passed on
questions.explanation: The resolution was adopted on 23 March 1940 on the concluding day of the League's Lahore session.

questions.text: The Lahore Resolution of 1940 was moved by
questions.explanation: A. K. Fazlul Haq, then Premier of Bengal, moved the resolution before the Lahore session.

questions.text: The Lahore session of the Muslim League in March 1940 was presided over by
questions.explanation: Jinnah presided over the Lahore session and in his address set out the case that Muslims were a nation by every definition.

questions.text: The Lahore Resolution was passed at which ground in Lahore?
questions.explanation: The session was held at Minto Park, now Iqbal Park, where the Minar-e-Pakistan later marked the spot.

questions.text: The Delhi Convention of Muslim League legislators in April 1946 amended the Lahore Resolution to demand
options: dominion status within the British Empire
a federation with India at the centre
a single independent state of Pakistan
questions.explanation: The 1946 convention replaced the wording about independent states with the demand for one sovereign state of Pakistan comprising the Muslim-majority zones.

questions.text: Which was the first provincial legislature in British India to pass a resolution in favour of Pakistan?
questions.explanation: The Sindh Legislative Assembly was the first to adopt a resolution supporting the demand for Pakistan.

questions.text: The Cripps Mission came to India in which year?
questions.explanation: Sir Stafford Cripps arrived in March 1942 with proposals meant to secure Indian support for the war effort.

questions.text: Who described the Cripps proposals as 'a post-dated cheque'?
questions.explanation: Gandhi dismissed the offer of dominion status after the war as a post-dated cheque, because nothing was to be conceded immediately.

questions.text: The Quit India Movement was launched in August of which year?
questions.explanation: The Congress passed the Quit India resolution in August 1942, after which its leadership was imprisoned for the rest of the war.

questions.text: The C. R. Formula of 1944 was an attempt to settle the deadlock between
options: the British government and the Congress
the Congress and the princely states
the Muslim League and the Sikhs
the Congress and the Muslim League
questions.explanation: C. Rajagopalachari's formula offered a plebiscite in the Muslim-majority districts in return for League cooperation, and formed the basis of the Gandhi-Jinnah talks.

questions.text: The Gandhi-Jinnah talks of September 1944 were held in which city?
questions.explanation: Gandhi met Jinnah at Jinnah's Bombay residence in September 1944, but the talks broke down over the definition of Pakistan.

questions.text: The Simla Conference of 1945 was convened by which Viceroy?
questions.explanation: Lord Wavell called the Simla Conference in June 1945 to form a new Executive Council of Indian members.

questions.text: The Simla Conference of 1945 failed mainly because of a disagreement over
options: the Muslim League's claim to nominate all Muslim members of the Executive Council
the date of British withdrawal from India
the future of the princely states
questions.explanation: Jinnah insisted that the League alone could nominate the Muslim members, a claim the Congress refused to accept, and the conference collapsed.

questions.text: In the elections to the Central Legislative Assembly held in 1945-46, the Muslim League won
options: twenty of the thirty Muslim seats
twenty-five of the thirty Muslim seats
questions.explanation: The League captured every one of the thirty Muslim seats in the central assembly, establishing its claim to speak for Indian Muslims.

questions.text: Who was the Viceroy of India when the Lahore Resolution was passed?
questions.explanation: Lord Linlithgow was Viceroy from 1936 to 1943 and therefore held office in March 1940.

questions.text: The Cabinet Mission reached India in which month and year?
questions.explanation: The three British ministers arrived in India in March 1946 to negotiate the transfer of power.

questions.text: The Cabinet Mission of 1946 was headed by
questions.explanation: Lord Pethick-Lawrence, the Secretary of State for India, led the mission as its senior member.

questions.text: The Cabinet Mission Plan was announced on
questions.explanation: The mission published its own plan on 16 May 1946 after the Simla talks between the Congress and the League failed.

questions.text: Into how many groups or sections did the Cabinet Mission Plan divide the provinces of British India?
questions.explanation: The plan placed the provinces in three sections, labelled A, B and C, within a loose federation.

questions.text: Under the Cabinet Mission Plan, Group B was to consist of
options: Bombay, Madras and the United Provinces
the Punjab, the North-West Frontier Province and Sindh
questions.explanation: Group B comprised the Muslim-majority provinces of the north-west, while Group C contained Bengal and Assam.

questions.text: The Muslim League observed Direct Action Day on
questions.explanation: Direct Action Day was observed on 16 August 1946 and was followed by severe rioting in Calcutta.

questions.text: The Muslim League called Direct Action Day after withdrawing its acceptance of
questions.explanation: The League withdrew its acceptance of the Cabinet Mission Plan when the Congress placed its own interpretation on the grouping clauses.

questions.text: The Interim Government took office on 2 September of which year?
questions.explanation: The Interim Government headed by Jawaharlal Nehru was sworn in on 2 September 1946, and the Muslim League joined it in October.

questions.text: Which portfolio did Liaquat Ali Khan hold in the Interim Government of 1946?
questions.explanation: Liaquat Ali Khan took charge of Finance and used the department to demonstrate the League's weight within the Interim Government.

questions.text: Prime Minister Attlee announced Britain's intention to transfer power in India by June 1948 on
questions.explanation: Attlee's statement of 20 February 1947 fixed a deadline for withdrawal and announced the appointment of a new Viceroy.

questions.text: Who was the last Viceroy of British India?
questions.explanation: Lord Mountbatten succeeded Lord Wavell in March 1947 and presided over the transfer of power.

questions.text: The plan for the partition of India announced on 3 June 1947 is also known as the
questions.explanation: The 3 June Plan, drawn up under Lord Mountbatten, provided the scheme by which British India was divided.

questions.text: Under the 3 June Plan a referendum was to be held in the North-West Frontier Province and in
questions.explanation: Referendums were prescribed for the North-West Frontier Province and for the Sylhet district of Assam.

questions.text: The referendum in the North-West Frontier Province was held in which month of 1947?
questions.explanation: The referendum took place in July 1947 and returned a large majority in favour of joining Pakistan, though the Khudai Khidmatgars boycotted it.

questions.text: The 1947 referendum in Sylhet resulted in the district joining
questions.explanation: Sylhet voted to leave Assam and join East Bengal, and so became part of Pakistan.

questions.text: The decision of British Balochistan to join Pakistan in 1947 was taken by
questions.explanation: The Shahi Jirga of Quetta, together with the non-official members of the Quetta municipality, voted in June 1947 for accession to Pakistan.

questions.text: The Indian Independence Act received the royal assent on
questions.explanation: The British Parliament passed the Indian Independence Act, which received the royal assent on 18 July 1947.

questions.text: Who was appointed chairman of the Punjab and Bengal Boundary Commissions?
questions.explanation: Sir Cyril Radcliffe chaired both boundary commissions, and the resulting line bears his name.

questions.text: The Radcliffe Award was made public on
questions.explanation: The boundary award was published on 17 August 1947, three days after Pakistan came into being.

questions.text: Apart from its chairman, each Boundary Commission of 1947 consisted of how many members?
questions.explanation: Each commission had four members, two nominated by the Congress and two by the Muslim League, so the chairman's casting voice decided every disputed point.

questions.text: Which Muslim-majority district was controversially awarded to India by the Radcliffe Award?
questions.explanation: Most of Gurdaspur district went to India despite its Muslim majority, giving India a land route to Kashmir.

questions.text: Pakistan came into being on
questions.explanation: Pakistan's independence was celebrated on 14 August 1947, the day the transfer of power took effect for the new dominion.

questions.text: Jinnah took the oath as the first Governor-General of Pakistan on
questions.explanation: Jinnah was sworn in as Governor-General on 15 August 1947, the day after the independence celebrations.

questions.text: Who was elected the first President of the Constituent Assembly of Pakistan?
questions.explanation: Jinnah was elected President of the Constituent Assembly on 11 August 1947 and delivered his celebrated address on that occasion.

questions.text: In his address to the Constituent Assembly on 11 August 1947 Jinnah stressed
options: freedom of religion for every citizen of the new state
the abolition of the princely states
the recovery of Kashmir by force
questions.explanation: Jinnah told the Assembly that every citizen was free to go to his temple or mosque and that religion had nothing to do with the business of the state.

questions.text: The Darul Uloom at Deoband was founded in 1866 by
questions.explanation: Maulana Muhammad Qasim Nanautvi established the seminary at Deoband in 1866 to preserve traditional Islamic learning after 1857.

questions.text: The Nadwatul Ulema was established in 1894 at
questions.explanation: The Nadwatul Ulema was founded at Lucknow with the aim of combining religious learning with modern subjects.

questions.text: The Anjuman-i-Himayat-i-Islam was founded in 1884 in which city?
questions.explanation: The Anjuman-i-Himayat-i-Islam was set up at Lahore to promote education among Muslims and to counter missionary activity.

questions.text: The Faraizi Movement in Bengal was founded by
questions.explanation: Haji Shariatullah began the Faraizi Movement in Bengal to make Muslims observe the obligatory duties of Islam and to resist landlord oppression.

questions.text: Syed Ahmad Barelvi was killed in 1831 in the battle of
questions.explanation: Syed Ahmad Barelvi and Shah Ismail Shaheed fell at Balakot in 1831 fighting the Sikh forces.

questions.text: The Indian National Congress was founded in 1885 with the help of
questions.explanation: Allan Octavian Hume, a retired British civil servant, took the leading part in organising the Congress in 1885.

questions.text: The Khudai Khidmatgar movement was founded by
questions.explanation: Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan organised the Khudai Khidmatgars, known as the Red Shirts, in the North-West Frontier Province and allied them with the Congress.

questions.text: Who was the first Muslim to preside over a session of the Indian National Congress?
questions.explanation: Badruddin Tyabji presided over the Congress session of 1887 at Madras, the first Muslim to hold that office.

questions.text: The Khaksar Movement was founded by
questions.explanation: Allama Inayatullah Khan Mashriqi founded the Khaksar Movement, whose members drilled with spades as a symbol of service and discipline.
